newsitem.title: USA: NYC's jobless rate trending down -- state labor.
newsitem.headline: NYC's jobless rate trending down -- state labor.

text.p: New York City's jobless rate fell nearly half a percentage point to back below 10 percent in April, the state Department of Labor said Tuesday, predicting the city's economy was on an upswing.
"We expect the rate to be trending downward," said Jim Brown, a state labor market analyst, who is based in New York City.
In April, the city's unemployment rate fell to 9.7 percent from 10.1 percent in March, which was about a three-year high.

New York State's unemployment rate dropped half a percentage point to 6.2 percent in April, partly due to the city's job growth, which benefited nearby areas, from Long Island to the Hudson Valley, Brown said.

Tourism and retail were the main sectors in New York City that hiring workers, he said. "The city is actually seeing very strong job growth. In the last 12 months, it added 60,000 private sector jobs.""

But the increases were not evenly spread, as New York County's 7.8 percent rate was lower than any other county in the city, with the jobless rate in the Bronx staying the highest in the city at 11.8 percent.

Upstate communities mostly have lower rates, though they have lagged on adding jobs, Brown said. The three upstate counties with the highest rates were: Hamilton, 14.8 percent, Franklin at 10.2 percent, and Essex at 10.1 percent.
A breakdown of New York City's job markets follows:
--New York, 7.8 percent, down from 8.1 percent in March. but up from 6.7 percent a year-ago.
--Bronx, 11.8 percent, down from 12.6 percent in March and 10.0 percent a year-ago.
--King's, 11.1 percent, down from 11.4 percent in March but up from 10.2 percent a year-ago.
--Queens, 9.0 percent, down from 9.4 percent in March but up from 8.3 percent a year-ago.
--Richmond, 8.4 percent, down from 8.6 percent in March but up from 7.8 percent a year-ago.
